svg.title: Dora client use through the workflow, cleanup and recovery
svg.desc: Planned Compose and systemd adoption: retained backend owners use one client through readiness, graph registration, observation and shutdown. Cancelled requests retain graph identity. Cleanup reconciles uncertain starts, destroys only after a confirmed stop, always verifies native exit and gates resource removal on stopped writers and durable evidence. Controller restart recovers from persisted native ownership.
svg.text: Dora client use, cleanup and recovery
Planned backend adoption · one client per experiment · typed JSON over a reused WebSocket
Step factories + ComposeRunning.resources retain the same owner
Dora retains the client; the running handle retains native unit ownership
Freeze descriptor, session and path facts
Retain native handles; no control RPC yet
Validate graph hash, ownership and endpoint
Record intent before the first await
Keep UUID before waiting for graph spawn
Use frozen dynamic graph + run/session ID
systemd: System phase, then User phase
Native application launch uses no client RPC
The same client is available to later steps
systemd retains the client while waiting
Read failure ends the applicable observation
Verify owned UUID, exact name and Running
User apps first, then system apps
Keep graph identity available for cleanup
Preserve system-node grace and drain order
Close socket on return; retain graph identity
Report node errors even after destruction
Native ownership remains until verified cleanup
Retain reports, artifacts and unresolved errors
Verify native exit and evidence durability
Drop the in-flight socket; keep the retained name / UUID. After cancelled startup, give cleanup a fresh stop budget.
Reconnect + Hello; List the exact run name
Use retained or uniquely recovered identity
The run still owns its native runtime
Skip graph stop; destroy the owned runtime
Confirmed node errors still permit Destroy
Keep node + Destroy errors; close the socket
Inspect, stop and verify owned resources
Verify process exit; preserve control errors
